messages:
marta: quick note — noticed a p99 tail after the kernel swap on prod-3 (rolled ~2h ago). p95 improved but p99 jumped. anyone else seeing this?

kevin: saw it in dashboards. p95 went from ~110ms -> ~78ms, p99 jumped from ~420ms -> ~900ms on batch-heavy traffic. traced to long queue delays for small requests.

devon: interesting — did the rollout change kernel selection heuristics? we pushed the new fused-attn kernel that favors large microbatches.

marta: yeah, kernel selector now biases heavy-attn ker nel for seq_len >= 512 and expects higher max_batch_tokens. but a lot of our requests are short (<=128) so microbatches are tiny and waiting longer to hit batch token threshold.

sam: KV-cache hit rate for that model spiked down during the window. looks like cache eviction / hotkey churn contributed to tail. hit_rate dropped from 88% -> 62% for a few minutes.

kevin: so two interacting effects: (1) kernel choice favors big batches, (2) scheduler max_batch_tokens causes longer waiting to form those batches, and (3) KV cache churn makes individual requests slower when they miss.

marta: agree. I ran a quick profiler on a repro node — attached snippet: 
```
# perf summary (sample)
seq<=128 microbatch: avg 52ms, p95 120ms, p99 750ms
seq 512+ microbatch: avg 260ms, p95 310ms, p99 360ms
queue_delay (ms): median 4, p95 210, p99 820
KV hit latency on miss: 14ms extra
```

devon: those queue_delay numbers match. p99 dominated by queue_delay, not kernel execution.

kevin: experiment idea: reduce max_batch_tokens for that model from 4096 -> 2048 and lower max_wait_ms from 10 -> 5 to cut queue tail. also add a short-seq fast-path that forces lightweight kernel selection for seq<=128.

marta: +1. also consider microbatch cap per request type (chat vs long-gen). We can route short chat to the legacy fast kernel even if it would theoretically pack into the fused kernel.

sam: added an ad-hoc A/B on a single host pool: control has old scheduler, variant uses max_batch_tokens=2048 and max_wait_ms=5 and fast-path for seq<=128. results after 30m: p95 slightly worse for long jobs (280 -> 300ms), but p99 for short requests down from 750 -> 210ms. overall tail SLA improved for our chat product.

marta: nice. what about throughput impact? did we lose QPS?

sam: throughput drop ~3% for that pool — acceptable tradeoff for tight p99 target. cost delta small.

devon: we should also tweak kernel_selector to consider current queue delay metrics (adaptive routing) rather than static seq_len thresholds. if queue_delay > 50ms, prefer fast kernel even for medium sequences.

kevin: exactly — adaptive kernel routing + scheduler backpressure. propose combined rule: if estimated added wait > expected exec delta, pick faster kernel. heuristics:
```
if queue_estimate_ms > exec_delta_ms * 0.7: route_to_low_latency_kernel
else: route_to_high_throughput_kernel
```

marta: will draft RFC for adaptive selector + per-model scheduler knobs. short-term: rollback kernel bias on prod-3 and deploy reduced max_batch_tokens/max_wait_ms on chat pool.

ops-bot: deploy started by @marta to cluster prod-3-chat-pool (task id: deploy-180234-9).

kevin: after deploy, monitor p95/p99, queue_delay heatmap, and KV hit rate. set alert if p99 > 500ms for 5m.

marta: noted. will also add a nightly job to simulate mixed short+long workload to catch regressions.

devon: follow-up experiment: add small per-slot reservation for hot keys to avoid KV eviction storms. might reduce miss spikes.

sam: logged follow-up tickets: INF-1268 (adaptive-kernel-selector), INF-1269 (scheduler-defaults-per-model), INF-1270 (kv-hotkey-reserve).

marta: thanks folks. plan: roll changes to canary, measure 1h, then wide. any objections?

kevin: go for canary. :thumbsup:

devon: +1

sam: deploying canary now.

ops-bot: canary deploy complete (prod-3-chat-pool). monitoring window started.

marta: closing thread — will post post-canary numbers in #eng-runtime later.
